source.title: A Mechanism Study of Delayed Loss Spikes in Batch-Normalized Linear Models
source.authors: Pei-Feng Gao; Wen-Yi Fang; Yang Zheng; Di-Fan Zou

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies delayed loss spikes in batch-normalized linear models, but does not test the classification-error, width, depth, initialization, learning-rate-stability, or training-speed claims in V1–V6.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses edge-of-stability work as context. Its own synthetic loss-trajectory results are recorded under fits_no_version because they do not measure the behaviors named in V1–V6.
record.test_reason: The study establishes a delayed directional-instability mechanism in batch-normalized linear models. It does not test V5's recovery relative to an initial linearized stability limit, sustained sharpness at the stability threshold, or divergence below that threshold. Its auxiliary sharpness curves do not establish these behaviors. It also does not measure the comparisons specified in V1–V4 or V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. More precisely, the whitened square-loss analysis establishes delayed directional onset and finite-time self-stabilization of the rising edge, with a square-loss interpretation; it does not prove eventual recovery to low loss. The logistic result is a restrictive finite-horizon directional precursor with a conditional exit threshold. Extension beyond whitening or to nonlinear architectures remains open.
record.recipe_differences: Full-batch gradient descent on batch-normalized linear models with synthetic data; the claim versions concern classification training error or other specified network training behaviors.
record.method_sensitivity: The theoretical results distinguish whitened square-loss regression from logistic regression under restrictive active-margin assumptions; the experiments use synthetic ill-conditioned data and show different evidential scope for the two losses.

fits_no_version.finding: For whitened square-loss batch-normalized linear regression, Theorems 2–3 give sufficient conditions for no directional rising edge or delayed onset, and finite-time termination of the rising edge through effective-learning-rate feedback. This does not establish eventual recovery to low training loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch normalization can create delayed directional instability that self-stabilizes in whitened square-loss linear regression.

fits_no_version.finding: The synthetic square-loss experiment shows a delayed loss increase coinciding with directional deviation and an effective-learning-rate rise and fall. The logistic experiment illustrates a directional transition; its theorem supplies only a restrictive finite-horizon precursor and conditional exit threshold.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalized linear models can exhibit delayed directional transitions, with stronger loss-spike evidence for square loss than for logistic loss.

record.problems: The numerical section is explicitly only a qualitative mechanism illustration, not comprehensive validation. It lacks a public code package, fixed random seeds, and a full hyperparameter table; the plotted numerical values are figure-only.

untested.parts: Training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels and the stated size, stopping, and regularization qualifications.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-dependent training degradation, identity shortcuts, and the specified initialization exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.

Recovery and divergence relative to the initial linearized stability limit in wide networks; sustained sharpness at the full-batch stability threshold; divergence despite starting below that threshold.
Accuracy gain and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, and Fixup's training-speed and stability comparison.

record.verdict_notes: No verdicts apply. The theoretical findings omitted from the rows concern a mechanism outside the supplied claim versions, so they are recorded under fits_no_version rather than missing.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR benchmarks, random or corrupted labels, model size, and stopping or regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and the effect of student width.
Depth, identity shortcuts, and training error in convolutional networks.
Initialization effects on signal propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.
The study does not compare learning rates with a linearized stability limit or track sharpness against the stability threshold in wide networks.
The study does not compare training speed or learning-rate tolerance with and without batch normalization.

rows.subject: batch-normalized linear model
rows.operation_detail: Full-batch gradient descent on synthetic data with square loss; the plotted trajectory illustrates a delayed loss increase.

conditions.value: Synthetic ill-conditioned data made by slicing a Hilbert matrix, applying random rotations, and adding Gaussian noise

rows.note: The text says the square-loss panel shows a visible delayed increase; precise values are only in the figure.
rows.check: The text explicitly reports a delayed square-loss increase, but that observation cannot determine any claim version's effect. Retain it as a finding outside the versions. The experiment uses ill-conditioned synthetic data; whitening is not established for this run despite Figure 3's caption invoking the whitened theorem regime.

rows.subject: batch-normalized linear model
rows.operation_detail: Full-batch gradient descent on synthetic data with logistic loss; the plotted trajectory illustrates a directional transition.

conditions.value: Synthetic ill-conditioned data made by slicing a Hilbert matrix, applying random rotations, and adding Gaussian noise

rows.note: The authors describe the panel as a qualitative directional illustration and say it is not evidence for a generic logistic spike claim; precise values are only in the figure.
rows.check: The authors report a qualitative directional transition, which the recorded loss-trajectory measure alone does not establish. Record the directional diagnostic separately if retaining this finding; neither it nor the reported loss trajectory establishes a claim version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
